decisions.reason: The candidate already requires moments that teach something or provide a real lesson. The source change adds narrative completeness and standalone understandability without necessarily changing that moment-value standard.

Narrative completeness does not change the candidate's clean-editing style or prohibited visual treatments; the source message's separate visual-editing clause is already represented by a same-message MODIFY.
Requiring a complete standalone lesson or story does not change the permitted source collection, source exclusions, or one-video batch constraint.
Narrative completeness does not alter the required caption font. The source message's independent font instruction is already represented by a same-message MODIFY.
The narrative-completeness change does not alter the assigned count or batch-delivery obligation. The separate instruction to redo all eight clips is already represented by a same-message MODIFY.
Narrative completeness does not change caption color or text-effect requirements. The source message's independent white-text-only rule is already represented by a same-message MODIFY.
A clip can require a complete standalone narrative without changing its opening-hook criterion, and the source does not explicitly revise hook selection.
The complete-story requirement does not revise the existing 20-to-120-second duration bounds.
The narrative-completeness standard does not change the monthly target of 180 approved clips or its counting basis.
